processing: Handled in the usual Darjeeling way for black tea: withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, lighter in spring and fuller in summer.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, first flush in spring, second flush in early summer and an autumn picking.
appearance_dry: Typical of whole-leaf Darjeeling: wiry leaf, greener in spring and browner with paler tips in summer.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in spring lots and bright amber in second flush.
appearance_wet: Mixed green and copper leaf, darker in later flushes.
taste_profile: Little documents one Jungpana flavour. Expect the Darjeeling arc of floral and brisk in spring, with rounder fruit in the summer flush.

brewing.notes: Western style. Cooler and shorter for spring lots, hotter for second flush.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and harvest year, like other named Darjeeling gardens, often through European tea houses. Drink spring lots within about a year. Ownership changed after 2017, so older reputations may not describe the latest lots.
description:
Jungpana is a very small Darjeeling garden in the Kurseong block, just 78 acres at 1,000 to 1,500 metres, with a reputation far larger than its size. Its tea has been sold by Fortnum & Mason and Harrods in Britain, and by Mariage Frères and Fauchon in France.

Nothing in its method is known to set it apart from other Darjeeling gardens. Flush, altitude and care in the factory shape what you get.

Brew it Western style and treat spring lots gently. Little is written about a single house taste, so a good seller's notes on the exact lot are more useful than the name.

With a small garden and a famous name, check the flush and year, and buy from a seller who can identify the lot.
history:
Henry Montgomery Lennox planted Jungpana in 1899. G.W. O'Brien later managed it and, after the Second World War, was forced to sell to the ruling Rana of Nepal. The Kejriwal family took over around 1956, and Shantanu Kejriwal, third generation, credited its overseas success to careful ownership.

After the 2017 strikes, businessman Sanjay Agarwal bought the estate and soon sold it on to the Santosh Kumar Kanoria Group.
